emails.subject: Invitation: End Semester Exhibition - The Self As We See It (VA-2016)
emails.body:
Dear All,

The Department of Visual Arts is delighted to invite you to the End Semester Exhibition for the course  VA-2016 - Figure Drawing as Remembering and Reimagining.

The Self As We See It
Date: 28th Nov 7 PM onwards & 29th November from 9AM - 9PM
Location: White Box (AC 04 fourth floor)
1000227646.jpg
We never see ourselves directly. We see ourselves through mirrors, photographs, memories, and other
people. This project aims to showcase learnings from the course Figure Drawing as Remembering
and Reimagining, which connects to the topic of seeing the self, remembered and
reimagined constantly.

‘As we see it’ points to the subjectivity of art and self-perception: the self is whatever we believe it to be
on a given day. But the “we” is also plural. These works are made by Anwesha and Karma, and reflect
their explorations of how the self is seen through our eyes and through each other's.

"The exhibition includes a range of works that seem quite diverse but are really parts of one
conversation: our self-portraits and earlier studies of other people where the idea of self can be seen too.
Drawing others taught us to slow down, observe closely, and reflect deeply. Looking back, we realised
we were often drawing ourselves: our emotions in someone’s posture, our thoughts in someone’s
expression, and a bit of our existence in that of others. The exhibition hopes to make that hidden
connection visible.

The project is driven by questions we do not expect to fully answer, but hope that it can take us a step
closer to understanding. Is a self-portrait a record of who we are, or of whom we wish to be seen as?
When we draw another person, how much of the drawing is them and how much is us? Can a stranger’s
face hold something of our own?"

We look forward to having you join us for the exhibition.
emails.rationale: Invites the campus community to a scheduled two-day art exhibition at White Box (AC 04).

emails.subject: Core Team Applications Open: RedBrick Hacks IV (Paid Roles)
emails.body:
Dear Students,

The organising team for  RedBrick Hacks IV  is expanding, and we're inviting members of the Ashoka student body to apply for two paid roles on this year's core team: UI/UX Designer and Content Creator.

RedBrick Hacks is Ashoka's flagship hackathon. In three editions it has grown from a 24-hour Delhi NCR hackathon into a national programme, with 437 applicants from 91+ universities across 23 states last year. RedBrick Hacks IV is hardware-first, and it needs creative people to shape how it looks and how it's talked about, from the first announcement to the last day.

We're looking for students who are:

- Creative, with an eye for detail and a love for good storytelling
- Reliable and proactive
- Comfortable working in fast-moving teams
- Interested in design, content creation or social media

Please share a portfolio of your work with your application, so we can see what you've made.

As a UI/UX Designer you would:

- Shape how RedBrick Hacks looks and feels across the website, posters, swag, slides and on-site signage
- Work closely with the core team so everything we put out looks like one event

As a Content Creator you would:

- Own content creation end to end: plan, script, shoot, edit, publish and post 
- Tell the RedBrick story through reels, videos, captions and announcements
- Build hype around the event, making people want to apply and show up
- Capture the event as it happens and share it across our channels

Interested students will first fill out the application form. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply early, as the positions may close once filled. Shortlisted applicants will then be invited for a brief interview, and final selections will be shared shortly after the interviews.

If this sounds like something you'd enjoy, please apply by Sunday, 29 November 2026 using the form below:

Application form: https://forms.gle/ZBpWeTTPbMJvKBmk8

If you have any questions, feel free to reply to this email.

Best wishes,
Team RedBrick Hacks

Digital Makerspace, Mphasis | AI Applied Tech Lab,  Ashoka
emails.rationale: Describes the RedBrick Hacks IV hackathon extensively, but the email itself is a hiring call for core team roles with an application deadline.

emails.subject: Fwd: Spring 2027 Course Registration - Demonstration Video
emails.body:
Dear Students,
We hope you are doing well and have gone through the Course Registration document shared with you earlier on November 18.
In continuation of our previous email, please find attached a step-by-step demonstration video of the new course registration process for your reference and better understanding.
We will share other relevant information and updates with you in a timely manner.
 New Registration Process.mp4

Regards
Team OAA

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 3:07 PM Office of Academic Affairs <oaa@ashoka.edu.in> wrote:
Dear Students,
We hope you are doing well.
We would like to inform you that, from the Spring 2027 semester, there will be a change in the course registration process. 
Context
Over many semesters, students have shared their concerns with the course registration process. Specifically, students had reported stress associated with the First-Come, First-Served (FCFS), or "fastest finger first" approach to course registration. The recent student survey indicates that 67% of students feel stressed on course registration day. While most students understand the registration process and they get most of the courses that they want, it is stressful to fight for seats in popular sections. 56% of students would like a new course registration process. We announce a new preference-based course allocation system, which reduces the time pressure of the current course registration system.
New Course Registration Process
Under the new system, instead of 2 rounds of registration, we will now have 4 rounds, which gives students multiple chances to find their desired courses. Course allocations will be made based on students' submitted preferences rather than the speed at which they register. The new system aims to provide students with greater flexibility and a more equitable course registration experience. 
The new course registration process will be conducted in the following rounds:
1. Round 1 – Course Selection -> This is the same as the current Pre-Registration Round
2. Round 2 – Oversubscribed Course Swap
3. Round 3 – Ranking and Alternatives for Oversubscribed Courses
4. Round 4(a) – Open Registration (Low-Credit Students)
5. Round 4(b) – Open Registration (All Students)


For further details about each round of the registration process, please find the attached document
The timelines for the Spring 2027 Registration will be shared shortly; please wait for our further communication.

Regards
Team OAA


--
Office of Academic Affairs
oaa@ashoka.edu.in T 01302300281 || www.ashoka.edu.in
Facebook | LinkedIn | Twitter | Virtual Tour

CAMPUS : PLOT: #2, Rajiv Gandhi Education City, P. O. Rai, Sonepat, Haryana 131 029

emails.subject: Colloquium Invitation: Inclusion for Entrenchment (Nov 25, 1:30 PM)
emails.body:
Hello everyone,

The Department of Political Science is delighted to invite you to attend the colloquium scheduled for Nov 25, 2026, at 01:30 PM. The details are as follows:

Title: Inclusion for Entrenchment: How Ruling Parties Subvert Electoral Quotas

Speaker: Anirvan Chowdhury
Time: 1:30 to 3:00  P.M. (IST)
Venue: LR - AC-04-LR-009

Nov 25.png
Abstract: Participation, contestation, and inclusion are regarded as mutually reinforcing pillars of democracy, yet institutional designs can generate trade-offs among them. Drawing on 180,432 Panchayat-level elections in West Bengal, India, we show that electoral quotas for marginalized groups reduce voter turnout and electoral competition, with especially pronounced effects under intersectional quotas. We trace these effects to institutional choices of partisan local elections and indirect executive selection, which create incentives and opportunities for ruling parties to capture reserved seats. Ruling parties suppress rival and internal contestation through coercion and co-optation. A survey experiment demonstrates how coercion induces voter exit. Our findings reveal how institutions designed to expand political inclusion can, under certain conditions, facilitate ruling-party contro
 
Bio:  Dr. Anirvan Chowdhury is an Assistant Professor of Political Science and the Aung San Suu Kyi Endowed Chair in Asian Democracy at the University of Louisville. His research focuses on the political economy of development, particularly in South Asia, with interests in religion, gender, party politics, and democratization.
His work examines how religiously conservative and nationalist political movements mobilize marginalized groups, particularly women, and the implications for political participation and democratic institutions. His research has been published in Science Advances and by Cambridge University Press, and has received several awards from the American Political Science Association.

Previously, he was a Postdoctoral Fellow at Harvard University's Weatherhead Center for International Affairs and a British Academy Visiting Fellow at King's College London. He received his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, in 2023.

Refreshments will be served at the venue. We look forward to having you with us.

Warm regards,
Department of Political Science
emails.rationale: Standard departmental colloquium invite with speaker, date, time, and AC-04 venue.

The Department of Economics is thrilled to share that Prof. Devika Roy has been awarded the 2026 Mahalanobis Memorial Medal by the Indian Econometric Society for her contributions to development economics and empirical labor studies.

Please join us in congratulating her on this well-deserved honor!

Warm regards,
Department of Economics
emails.rationale: Congratulatory announcement of a faculty award, no event scheduled.

emails.subject: Cab Share to IGI Airport Terminal 3 on Dec 18 (6:00 AM Departure)
emails.body:
Hey everyone,

Looking for 2 people to split an Innova cab from Campus Main Gate to Delhi Airport T3 on Friday, December 18 at 6:00 AM (my flight is at 9:15 AM).

Total fare is ₹1,800 split 3 ways (₹600 each). Text me at 99102XXXXX if you're on a morning flight too!

Best,
Rohan (UG '28)
emails.rationale: Contains a specific date and departure time, so it looks event-like at a glance, but is a personal airport cab-sharing request.

emails.subject: Academic Integrity Reminder Ahead of Final Papers & Take-Home Exams
emails.body:
Dear Students,

As you submit final term papers and take-home examinations, please review the Ashoka University Academic Integrity Policy. All written submissions are screened via Turnitin, and unauthorized use of generative AI tools where prohibited by the course syllabus constitutes an integrity violation.

When in doubt about citation rules, consult your instructor or the Centre for Writing and Communication (CWC) guide.

Regards,
Office of Academic Affairs
emails.rationale: Academic policy reminder regarding plagiarism and final papers.

emails.subject: Full-Time Role: Associate Product Manager at Razorpay (Bengaluru) - Apply by Dec 4
emails.body:
Dear Graduating Batch,

Razorpay is hiring Associate Product Managers (APM) from the Class of 2027.

- Location: Bengaluru
- Compensation: ₹18 LPA + ESOPs
- Selection Process: Resume shortlisting -> Product Deck submission -> 2 online PM interviews
- Apply on Superset before Friday, 4 December 2026, 11:59 PM.

Regards,
Career Development Office
emails.rationale: Full-time job posting with deadline, no scheduled session.

emails.subject: ACWB Exam-Period 1-on-1 Counseling Appointment Availability & Crisis Helpline
emails.body:
Dear Students,

During December reading and examination weeks, the Ashoka Centre for Well-Being continues to offer confidential 1-on-1 counseling appointments (in-person and Zoom) Monday through Saturday, 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM.

Book an individual appointment via the ACWB portal, or call our 24x7 crisis support line at +91-130-2300-999 anytime.

Warmly,
Ashoka Centre for Well-Being
emails.rationale: Informational notice about regular clinic hours and emergency helpline numbers, not a scheduled group event.

emails.subject: Holiday List 2027: Official University Gazetted & Restricted Holidays
emails.body:
Dear Faculty, Staff, and Students,

Please find attached the official Ashoka University Holiday Calendar for the calendar year 2027.

Ashoka_Holiday_Calendar_2027.pdf

Essential campus services including Security, Infirmary, Residence Life, and Main Mess will remain operational on all holidays.

Regards,
Human Resources Department
emails.rationale: Administrative distribution of the annual holiday PDF.

emails.subject: Vote Now: Pick Our End-Semester Midnight Screening Movie!
emails.body:
Hey movie buffs,

Help us decide what we screen for our final Friday night screening next week! Vote between:
- Everything Everywhere All At Once
- Past Lives
- Knives Out
- Gangs of Wasseypur (Part 1)

Cast your vote before tomorrow 6 PM: https://forms.gle/filmPollDec

Ashoka Film Society
emails.rationale: Hard edge case: sent by Film Society and mentions a future screening, but this email is purely an online poll asking people to vote on a movie title without a scheduled date/time/venue yet.

emails.subject: Safety Notice: Autoclave & Biosafety Cabinet Certification in AC-04 Wet Labs
emails.body:
Dear Lab Users and PhD Scholars,

Annual third-party calibration of Biosafety Cabinets in AC-04 Labs 302 and 305 will take place on Monday, 30 November 2026, from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM.

Please pause cell culture work in those hoods during the inspection window.

Regards,
Lab Safety Committee, Department of Biology
emails.rationale: Lab equipment calibration notice.

emails.subject: Hiring: Student Social Media & YouTube Vloggers for Admissions (Paid Part-Time)
emails.body:
Dear Students,

The Office of Admissions is looking for 4 undergraduate content creators to film 'Day in the Life at Ashoka' videos and dorm tours for prospective applicants.

- Stipend: ₹4,000 per approved video
- Commitment: 2 videos per month in Spring 2027
- Apply with a sample reel link by Dec 5: https://forms.gle/admissionsCreators27

Office of Admissions
emails.rationale: Paid part-time student creator recruitment call.

emails.subject: Reminder: Register Overnight Guests on MyAshoka 24 Hours in Advance
emails.body:
Dear Residents,

Per the Residence Life Guest Policy, parents or external visitors staying in the campus guest house or visiting residence common areas must be pre-registered on the MyAshoka Gate Pass portal at least 24 hours prior to arrival.

Unregistered visitors will not be issued day passes at Gate 1.

Regards,
Residence Life & Campus Security
emails.rationale: Routine policy reminder about visitor gate passes.

emails.subject: Congratulations to 48 Students Placed in Cycle 0 Consulting & Finance Offers!
emails.body:
Dear Ashoka Community,

We are delighted to share that 48 students from the Class of 2027 have received full-time offers during Cycle 0 across BCG, Bain, Alvarez & Marsal, Deutsche Bank, and Nomura.

We thank faculty mentors and alumni interviewers for supporting our students throughout preparation.

Warm regards,
Career Development Office
emails.rationale: Announcement celebrating student placement results.

emails.subject: RedBrick Hacks III Winner Spotlight: Meet the Team Behind 'BrailleLens'
emails.body:
Hey Ashoka,

Before we kick off RedBrick Hacks IV next semester, check out our blog spotlight on last edition's Grand Prize winners—a 3-person sophomore team from Ashoka and IIIT-Delhi who built an offline tactile OCR reader on a Raspberry Pi Zero!

Read their build log & GitHub repo here: https://redbrickhacks.in/blog/braillelens

Team RedBrick Hacks
emails.rationale: Hard edge case: mentions RedBrick Hacks and winners, but is a blog newsletter spotlighting a past hackathon project rather than inviting readers to an upcoming event.
